title: Governance Failure Autopsy: A Technical Analysis of Documented AI Incidents

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a governance failure taxonomy enables targeted intervention design and fills a gap explicitly identified in the International AI Safety Report 2026.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: coding incidents along multiple governance dimensions requires careful reading and judgment, manageable with guidance but not trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: 30-50 incidents each requiring multi-dimensional coding is substantial but has clear methodology and stopping criteria.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple incident taxonomies exist covering technical failures, risk mitigation, and multi-dimensional cause analysis. However, the specific governance failure analysis angle -- coding incidents along governance mechanism dimensions to identify where governance infrastructure failed -- adds differentiation from the predominantly technical failure taxonomies. The governance-specific lens is partially novel.

evidence: Rui et al. (arXiv:2211.07280) 'A taxonomic system for failure cause analysis of open source AI incidents' provides technical failure cause taxonomy applied to AIID
arXiv:2603.04259 (March 2026) 'When AI Fails, What Works?' provides data-driven taxonomy of risk mitigation strategies from AI incidents
arXiv:2504.01029 maps causes, entities, and consequences of AI privacy/ethical incidents with multi-dimensional classification
Root cause analysis tools have been applied to AI safety incidents (Mylius 2025)
arXiv:2603.06847 provides fault taxonomy for agentic AI with 5 fault dimensions, 13 symptom classes, 12 root cause categories
